facts.statement: Fasolasuchus fossils were discovered in the Los Colorados Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina

facts.statement: The genus name Fasolasuchus honors Tomás H. Fasola, who found the specimen and collaborated on Bonaparte's expeditions to the Triassic of Argentina.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico fue dedicado a Tomás H. Fasola, quien halló el espécimen y colaborara en las expediciones de Bonaparte al Triásico de Argentina.

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina that date back to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus existed between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus is classified as an extinct genus of loricatan.
facts.quote: Fasolasuchus is an extinct genus of loricatan.

facts.statement: A 2011 study by Nesbitt provided a cladogram placing Fasolasuchus within its evolutionary context.
facts.quote: Cladograma según un estudio de Nesbitt en 2011:

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus is considered the largest known non-dinosaurian terrestrial predator.
facts.quote: making it the largest non-dinosaurian terrestrial predator known

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus is estimated to have reached a length of 8 to 10 meters.
facts.quote: Fasolasuchus is likely the largest known rauisuchian, with an estimated length of 8 - 10 m

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus is estimated to have weighed 1.6 tons and measured between 7.6 meters in length.
facts.quote: con una longitud estimada de entre 7.6 metros de longitud y 1.6 toneladas

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus possessed two rows of osteoderms along its back.
facts.quote: It had two rows of osteoderms along its back

facts.statement: Unlike most rauisuchians, Fasolasuchus had only a single row of osteoderms on its tail.
facts.quote: it had only a single row on the tail, unusual among rauisuchians

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus had a hyposphene-hypantrum articulation that provided extra rigidity to its vertebral column.
facts.quote: It also had a hyposphene-hypantrum articulation that gave the vertebral column extra rigidity.

facts.statement: The known Fasolasuchus specimen was somatically and skeletally mature, but its sexual maturity could not be determined.
facts.quote: the specimen was somatically and skeletally mature, but it wasn't possible to determine sexual maturity

facts.statement: In the holotype specimen, the femur measures 70 cm in length, which is double the length of the fibula.
facts.quote: In the smaller individual (the holotype), the femur is 70 cm in length, double that of the fibula.

facts.statement: Fasolasuchus fossils found in Argentina date to the Rhaetian stage of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles han sido hallados en Argentina y datan de la etapa del Rhaetiense del Triásico Superior
